explanation: The dorsal column tracts (gracile and cuneate) carry conscious proprioception and fine touch. The lateralmost fibers in the dorsal column represent sacral segments, which ascend most medially in the spinal cord.
keyConcept: Sacral fibers are most lateral in dorsal columns

explanation: Crude touch and pressure are carried by the ventral (anterior) spinothalamic tract. Pain and temperature are carried by the lateral spinothalamic tract, while fine touch uses the dorsal columns.
keyConcept: Ventral spinothalamic carries crude touch

explanation: Pain from the face travels via the trigeminal nerve. The first order neuron cell bodies are in the trigeminal ganglion, second order neurons are in the spinal nucleus of the trigeminal nerve in the brainstem.
keyConcept: Spinal nucleus of CN V carries face pain 2nd neuron

explanation: Recognizing a familiar object by touch (stereognosis) requires fine touch and proprioception, carried by the cuneate tract from the upper limb. The gracile tract carries these sensations from the lower body.
keyConcept: Cuneate tract carries fine touch from upper limb

explanation: The spinothalamic tracts show somatotopic organization where sacral fibers are most lateral (superficial) and cervical fibers are most medial (deep). This arrangement is preserved as fibers ascend through the brainstem.
keyConcept: Sacral fibers are most lateral in spinothalamic tract

explanation: The gracile tract conveys proprioceptive and fine touch sensations from the lower half of the body. It carries impulses from T7 spinal segment and below, with its fibers passing medially to the cuneate tract.
keyConcept: Gracile tract carries proprioception from lower body

explanation: The cuneate tract begins at the C8 spinal segment and carries conscious proprioception and fine touch from the upper limb. It does not start at mid-thoracic region—that level marks the beginning of the gracile tract.
keyConcept: Cuneate tract starts at C8, carries upper limb proprioception

explanation: The medial lemniscus is formed by second order neurons of the dorsal column pathway (gracile and cuneate). It carries conscious proprioception and fine touch from the contralateral side of the body.
keyConcept: Medial lemniscus carries contralateral fine touch/proprioception

explanation: Conscious proprioception from the right lower limb is carried by the right gracile tract, which ascends ipsilaterally in the posterior column and decussates in the medulla.
keyConcept: Gracile tract is ipsilateral for lower limb proprioception

explanation: Unconscious proprioception, which does not reach conscious awareness, is carried to the cerebellum by the anterior and posterior spinocerebellar tracts.
keyConcept: Spinocerebellar tracts carry unconscious proprioception

explanation: The lateral spinothalamic tract carries pain and temperature sensations. The ventral spinothalamic carries crude touch, while the dorsal columns carry fine touch, vibration, and proprioception.
keyConcept: Lateral spinothalamic carries pain and temperature

explanation: The spinal lemniscus is formed by fibers of the spinothalamic tracts after they decussate. Pain and temperature from the left body crosses to the right spinal lemniscus.
keyConcept: Spinal lemniscus carries contralateral pain/temperature

explanation: The postcentral gyrus is the primary somatosensory cortex. It receives pain and temperature via the spinothalamic pathway, but does not receive muscle tone, which is a motor function.
keyConcept: Postcentral gyrus processes sensory modalities except motor tone

explanation: The ventral spinothalamic tract decussates at the spinal cord level (not medulla) before ascending. It carries crude touch and pressure, lies in the anterior white column, and terminates in VPL of thalamus.
keyConcept: Ventral spinothalamic decussates at spinal cord level

explanation: Sense of movement (kinesthesia) and position sense are carried by the dorsal column tracts (gracile and cuneate). Loss of these sensations indicates damage to the posterior columns.
keyConcept: Gracile and cuneate tracts carry position/movement sense

explanation: The cuneate tract carries fine (discriminative) touch from the upper limb only. Crude touch from upper limb is carried by the ventral spinothalamic tract. Lower limb fine touch uses the gracile tract.
keyConcept: Cuneate tract carries fine touch from upper limb only

explanation: The left spinal lemniscus carries pain and temperature from the right side of the body (after decussation). Fine touch and proprioception use the medial lemniscus, not the spinal lemniscus.
keyConcept: Spinal lemniscus carries contralateral crude sensation

explanation: The gracile tract carries sensations from the lower body. Sacral fibers are most medial (closest to the midline), while cervical fibers are most lateral in this tract.
keyConcept: Sacral fibers are most medial in gracile tract

explanation: Fine touch and conscious proprioception from the upper limb (position sense) do not synapse in the spinal cord; their first order neurons pass directly to the dorsal column nuclei in the medulla.
keyConcept: Dorsal column sensations bypass spinal synapse

explanation: A lesion in the right gracile tract affects proprioception and fine touch from the right lower limb. Vibration sense testing of the right tibia would be diminished because this tract carries vibration sense.
keyConcept: Gracile tract lesion affects ipsilateral lower limb vibration

explanation: The first order neuron for pain from the face is the pseudounipolar neuron in the trigeminal ganglion. Its peripheral process receives pain from the face, and central process enters the brainstem.
keyConcept: Trigeminal ganglion is 1st neuron for face pain

explanation: Axons of the cuneate nucleus carry conscious proprioception from the thumb and upper limb. The error here is saying VPMN receives spinal lemniscus—VPM receives somatosensory input from the face via the trigeminal pathway, while VPL receives spinal input.
keyConcept: Cuneate nucleus axons carry upper limb proprioception

explanation: This matching question tests knowledge of sensory pathways. The lateral spinothalamic tract contains the second order neuron for pain from the lower limb, while VPMN is the third order neuron for pain from the face.
keyConcept: Lateral spinothalamic 2nd neuron for body pain

explanation: This matching tests understanding of ascending tracts. The cuneocerebellar tract begins from the accessory cuneate nucleus and carries unconscious proprioception from cervical segments to the cerebellum.
keyConcept: Accessory cuneate nucleus starts cuneocerebellar tract

explanation: Fine touch pathway: 1st neuron (dorsal root ganglion) ascends in dorsal columns to gracile/cuneate nuclei; 2nd neuron decussates as internal arcuate fibers and ascends in medial lemniscus (not spinal lemniscus) to VPL (not VPM) of thalamus.
keyConcept: Fine touch uses medial lemniscus, not spinal lemniscus

explanation: In the gracile tract, sacral fibers are located most medially (near the posterior median sulcus) while cervical fibers are most lateral. This somatotopic arrangement is maintained throughout the tract.
keyConcept: Sacral fibers most medial in gracile tract
